This method builds on [Voxel Space Setup](3520-voxel-space-setup.md) by utilizing the established transformation matrices to perform efficient, incremental coordinate calculations [S1].

The claim states that the method utilizes established transformation matrices to perform efficient, incremental coordinate calculations. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly describes an 'incremental algorithm' used to determine voxel positions without heavy computations. It details the use of rotation equations (transformation matrices) involving sin(theta) and cos(theta) to back-rotate coordinates from destination to source. Furthermore, it highlights that these calculations employ 'only two fixed-point additions that can be performed in parallel,' which supports the description of the calculations as 'efficient.' All specific facts mentioned in the claim are present in the evidence.

* **Input:** Destination voxel grid dimensions, rotation angle $\theta$ (about the Z-axis), and the source voxel data structure [S1].

The claim lists specific inputs (destination voxel grid dimensions, rotation angle theta, source voxel data structure) and describes the algorithmic steps found in Source [S1]. The source text explicitly mentions: 1) Rotation about the Z-axis, 2) The use of back-rotation to eradicate holes produced by forward rotation, 3) Rotating the eight corners of the source room to locate the destination room, 4) Back-rotating minimum coordinates using -theta, 5) Using an incremental procedure with sin(theta) and cos(theta) increments, 6) The specific coordinate equations (Equations 11-14 in the text match the claim's formulas), 7) The use of parallel memory/barrel shifters for beams parallel to the axis, and 8) Overcoming overlap by starting the scan at the source vertex within the destination room. All facts in the claim are present in the evidence.
